headline: ONE THIRD OF YOUTUBE ADVERTISING REVENUE NOW COMES FROM PEOPLE WATCHING ON A TELEVISION SET, AND ALPHABET NAMED BRAND PARTNERSHIPS RATHER THAN VIEWS AS THE BIGGEST SINGLE CONTRIBUTION TO ITS ADVERTISING GROWTH

tldr: Alphabet says living-room television viewing now accounts for a third of all YouTube advertising revenue, and named deeper brand partnerships rather than reach as the largest single contribution to its advertising growth — on a quarter where YouTube advertising rose about 9 percent to 11.21 billion dollars, the slowest growth it has posted this year.  Cast your last five YouTube deliverables to an actual television this week and fix the captions you cannot read, the dialogue the music walks over and the cuts that feel frantic from a sofa.

All 30 brands in iSpot's third-quarter panel converted at a higher rate on streaming than on ordinary television — 3.49 percent against 0.69 percent over fourteen days — and 15 of those same 30 still got more total conversions out of ordinary television, because it carried 78 percent of the impressions for 51 percent of the money.  Put conversion rate and total conversions in adjacent columns in your own reporting, because the two will rank your channels differently and that disagreement is the real decision.

Forty percent of views and 30 percent of clicks on YouTube microdramas arrive more than 30 days after the video goes live, which means the standard fourteen-day post-campaign read on any episodic video is measuring about half the audience.  Write a 60-day measurement window into your next serialised project before anyone shoots, and keep promotion running past day 30 instead of front-loading it all into launch week.

Google's claimed conversion lift for creator advertising rose from 20 percent to 30 percent on an identical dataset and identical date range, and yesterday's holiday guide repeats the 30 percent with no source note attached at all.  Run one genuine holdout test on creator boosting this quarter and approve the budget on your own number, and make a rule that a performance figure without a source note does not go in a deck.

Eighty-eight percent of the hours watched for Monday's Ballon d'Or went to watch parties rather than the official feed, DAZN Football took about 11.2 percent despite holding the rights, and the overall peak of 4.66 million concurrent viewers arrived after its broadcast had finished — with no average concurrent figure published for anything.  Contract average concurrent viewers as the measure on every live sponsorship, and ask what share of the hours is expected to come from watch parties and whether your branding appears on them.

The head of Instagram said on the record that the video creator payments the platform already makes lose it money and that monetisation is not a short-term priority, in the same week it is asking creators for 90-minute uploads with no revenue share.  Price any Instagram long-form series as a full commission with no platform subsidy underneath it, and check this week that you hold the rights to post the same cut on YouTube.

Global advertising spend is heading for 1.34 trillion dollars this year with social up 21.3 percent in the third quarter, one agency reports client budgets up as much as 20 percent in the fourth quarter with most of it going to social, and the biggest platform's own growth has slowed to 9 percent.  Make your sales calls this week rather than in November, and get fourth-quarter rates confirmed in writing along with what they become the week after the election.
